The TRICARE payment delays are a disgrace—another example of bureaucratic incompetence hitting military families hardest. While the Pentagon burns through $820 billion annually, they can’t process claims for kids’ physical therapy or behavioral health services? Small clinics owed $100k+ are collapsing, and D.C.’s answer is more paperwork. 

H.R. 873 tried to streamline reimbursement rates, but the real issue is the Defense Health Agency’s failure to execute. If agencies can’t handle basic payments, why are taxpayers funding their bloat? Veterans earned better than this circus. 

Cut the red tape, reimburse providers, and fire the bureaucrats who let this happen. Accountability starts with efficient systems, not empty promises.

The OBBB claims fiscal responsibility but falls short where it matters. While securing the border and military funding are non-negotiable priorities, the bill’s $1.6T in cuts barely scratch the surface of the $6T needed to reverse Biden-era bloat. Section 3’s Medicaid "strengthening" looks more like padding for pharma middlemen than real reform—block grants tied to drug price transparency would save $200B+ alone.

The rushed 1,100-page drafting process reeks of the same D.C. insider games, with loopholes like SALT cap expansions ($200B/yr revenue loss) undermining deficit claims. Until the Senate strips out special interest carve-outs and replaces “cost-plus” defense contracts with fixed-price models ($150B savings), this isn’t fiscal responsibility—it’s theater.

America deserves actual accountability, not recycled failures.

But let’s not pretend this solves systemic waste. The bill’s own projections show it cuts just $1.6 trillion while adding up to $5.8 trillion in new debt.

The One Big Beautiful Bill’s Medicaid “reforms” are classic D.C. theater—trimming pennies while burning dollars. Cutting retroactive coverage and hunting deceased enrollees might save $17B, but it ignores the $863B elephant in the room: a system rigged to funnel cash to pharmaceutical middlemen and billing consultants.

Until we block-grant Medicaid, slash redundant admin layers, and jail the fraudsters exploiting $50B in annual improper payments, these “integrity” measures are just bureaucratic virtue signaling.

Fix the structure, not the symptoms.
